findings.title: 种子共享 seed-data 模块的推荐写法在进程内测试路径下解析失败
findings.detail: nocobase-app-plugin-authorization/references/code-and-seeds.md 建议种子 `import { engineer } from '../../seed-data/permission-sets.js'`。但 seed 由 @nocobase/db 的 importTaskDefinition 加载：CLI 下走 tsx 可把 .js 解析到 .ts，进程内测试则由 Node 原生类型剥离直接加载，相对 ./x.js 不会解析到 x.ts。该函数只对入口文件调用 __rewriteRelativeImportExtension，不处理种子内部的相对导入。
findings.impact: 按指引编写的种子会在“真实测试库”路径下报 Cannot find module，作者被迫内联共享常量，削弱复用并增加重复。
findings.suggestedChange: 把示例改为跨路径可加载的写法（无扩展名或显式 .ts 说明），或在 @nocobase/db 的任务加载器中对传递依赖同样做 TS 扩展名解析。

diagnosis.trigger: 按 code-and-seeds.md 示例在 seed 中导入 ../../seed-data/*.js。
diagnosis.expected: 同一种子在 CLI、dev server 与进程内测试三条路径下都能加载。
diagnosis.actual: 进程内测试路径下报 Cannot find module '.../seed-data/expense-permission-sets.js'；db 仅改写入口文件扩展名。
diagnosis.workaround: 把共享声明内联进单个种子（本项目已在 202610010011_expense_departments.ts 中内联并注释原因）。
diagnosis.acceptance: 示例更新为可跨路径加载，或加载器对传递依赖执行同等解析，且新增回归测试覆盖进程内测试路径。

findings.title: createAppTest 不提供 auth.secret，testing.md 示例照抄即启动失败

findings.impact: Agent 按文档编写整应用测试时需要额外排查启动失败原因，测试基础设施的开箱可用性不足。
findings.suggestedChange: 测试库在未显式提供时为测试应用生成/注入一个 secret，或在示例与类型中强制展示该必需配置。

diagnosis.trigger: 按 testing.md 示例调用 createAppTest({ createServer: createStandaloneServer })。
diagnosis.expected: 示例开箱即可启动一个已配置认证的测试应用。
diagnosis.actual: 测试库不生成 auth.secret，认证插件启动期报缺少 secret（应用未配置）。
diagnosis.workaround: 在 createAppTest({ config: { auth: { secret: '...' } } }) 中显式提供。
diagnosis.acceptance: 测试库自动注入测试 secret，或文档示例明确展示该配置并通过一条整应用测试。

findings.title: 测试登录助手缺 Origin，cookie 写请求被 CSRF 校验拒绝
findings.detail: app-plugin-authentication/testing.js 的 signIn()/TestSession 返回的 fetch 会带上 cookie，但不设置 Origin 头；而同插件的 checkCookieWriteOrigin 要求携带 cookie 的非只读请求必须带可信 Origin/Referer，否则返回 403 INVALID_CSRF_ORIGIN。已在测试输出中观察到 create 请求以 403 失败。
findings.impact: 用测试助手调写接口的测试会在 CSRF 层失败，掩盖真正的业务断言，并消耗 Agent 排查时间。
findings.suggestedChange: TestSession.fetch 默认发送 TEST_ORIGIN（或在类型/文档中明确要求调用方设置），使测试会话与浏览器同源写请求一致。

diagnosis.trigger: 用 signIn() 得到的会话 fetch 发起 POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE。
diagnosis.expected: 测试会话的写请求与浏览器一致，通过 CSRF 校验。
diagnosis.actual: 写请求无 Origin，被 checkCookieWriteOrigin 判为不可信来源并返回 403 INVALID_CSRF_ORIGIN。
diagnosis.workaround: 在测试请求头中手动加 Origin: http://localhost。
diagnosis.acceptance: 测试助手默认发送可信 Origin，并有覆盖 cookie 写请求的回归测试。

feedbackReview.reason: 定向复核未完成：Pi invocation timed out after 180 seconds.

findings.title: testing.md 示例使用裸 expect，与模板 vitest 配置（未开 globals）不一致
findings.detail: testing.md 的整应用测试示例直接使用裸 expect(...)，而 app/vitest.config.ts 未设置 globals:true。测试运行时报 ReferenceError: expect is not defined。

findings.suggestedChange: 示例统一 `import { expect } from 'vitest'`，或在模板 vitest 配置开启 globals 并在指引中说明。

diagnosis.trigger: 按 testing.md 示例写测试并使用裸 expect。
diagnosis.expected: 示例在模板默认 vitest 配置下即可运行。
diagnosis.actual: 模板未开启 globals，示例未导入 expect，报 ReferenceError: expect is not defined。

processNotes.author: implementer
processNotes.summary: Built the whole expense reimbursement feature (schema, service, API, pages, seeds, tests) from scratch; the business code itself went smoothly and most of the time went into making the in-process test harness boot — seed loading, CSRF origin, and the public base path — and into the final lint sweep. Repair round 1 fixed the frozen-lockfile drift caused by moving the shadcn-added client packages to devDependencies in package.json without regenerating pnpm-lock.yaml.

blockers.title: A source seed that imports another source .ts file through a .js specifier fails on the in-process test path
blockers.symptom: Running the app through `createAppTest` (install: true) failed to load the seed graph; the shared `./expense-permission-sets.js` specifier did not resolve to its `.ts` source. The same graph loaded fine under `tsx` from the CLI.
blockers.rootCause: `importTaskDefinition()` imports the seed file with a `?mtime` URL and rewrites only the entry file's own relative `.js` extension. A relative `./x.js` specifier from a seed is not rewritten, and the vitest in-process app-test path imports the raw TypeScript with plain Node native type stripping, where `./x.js` is a literal, missing file.
blockers.resolution: Made every expense seed self-contained: the permission-set declaration was inlined into `202610010011_expense_departments.ts`, the `database/seed-data/expense-permission-sets.ts` module was deleted, and a comment in the seed explains why.
blockers.cost: One refactor of the seeds plus one test round (~20 min); the constraint was only discovered when the API test first installed the app.

blockers.title: Cookie-authenticated writes in the app-test harness are rejected as INVALID_CSRF_ORIGIN
blockers.symptom: POST/PATCH requests sent by `TestSession.fetch` were answered `403` with reason `INVALID_CSRF_ORIGIN`, even though the session cookie was present.
blockers.rootCause: `checkCookieWriteOrigin` resolves an origin from `Origin`/`Referer` and rejects a cookie write whose origin is missing or not trusted. `TestSession.fetch` adds no `Origin`, and `createAppTest` config had no `auth.trustedOrigins`. Adding only the request header was not enough; the origin must also be in the trusted list.
blockers.resolution: The API test passes `config: { app: { publicOrigin: TEST_ORIGIN }, auth: { trustedOrigins: [TEST_ORIGIN] } }` and every write goes through a `write()` helper that sets `content-type: application/json` and `origin: TEST_ORIGIN`.
blockers.cost: About 3 debug rounds and ~15 minutes before the two-part requirement (header plus trusted list) was clear.

blockers.title: Manually built request URLs must include the application public base path
blockers.symptom: `fetch(new Request('http://localhost/uploads/...'))` returned a bare `404 Not found`; `/api/...` requests through `testApp.request()` worked.
blockers.rootCause: The standalone server wraps the application in `createPublicBasePathAdapter`, which answers any pathname that does not start with `app.publicBasePath` (i.e. `/main`) with a 404. `testApp.request()` already prefixes `publicBasePath`, but a root-level file URL built by hand does not.
blockers.resolution: Root-level URLs are built as `` `http://localhost${testApp.publicBasePath}/uploads/expenseInvoices/...` ``; the test destructures `testApp` instead of reading a `publicBasePath` viTest fixture (which does not exist and yields `undefined`).
blockers.cost: One debug round (~10 min); the 404 looked like a routing bug rather than a mounting detail.

blockers.title: The file plugin's content route is public by design, so private invoices would be readable by anyone with a UUID
blockers.symptom: The route `defineFileRepositoryApiRoutes` generates for `${accessPath}/:file` served file content without requiring a session.
blockers.rootCause: The file plugin documents the content route as UUID-addressed and intentionally unauthenticated; it is meant to be embedded in contexts where the UUID is the capability.
blockers.resolution: The route contribution wraps only the owned `${accessPath}/*` prefix with an app-owned `auth.required()` middleware, and `server/AGENTS.md` records that claim-level byte authorization beyond possession of the UUID is a deliberate limitation. Per-claim authorization for the bytes remains a documented gap.
blockers.cost: One design detour (~15 min); the private-invoice requirement would otherwise have been silently violated.

blockers.title: ExpenseProvider.start() broke embedded hosts that mount the runtime without this app's migrations
blockers.symptom: Two `tests/logic/app-server.test.ts` failures: `RepositoryError: Collection "expenseExportJobs" does not exist.` in embedded test scopes that create a temp app root with no `database/` migrations.
blockers.rootCause: Startup resume called `listUnfinishedExportJobs()` unconditionally; an embedded host can legitimately mount the runtime before/without the application schema.
blockers.resolution: `listUnfinishedExportJobs()` returns `[]` when the `expenseExportJobs` collection is absent, so the provider boots on a schema-less runtime.

blockers.title: createAppTest requires an explicit auth secret, which the app never ships with a default
blockers.symptom: `ApplicationNotConfiguredError: auth.secret is not set.` when starting the app-test server.
blockers.rootCause: `resolveAuthSecret` throws when no secret is configured, by design; `createAppTest` does not synthesise one.
blockers.resolution: The expense API test passes a test-only `auth.secret`. Recorded so the next feature test does not rediscover it.

blockers.title: Lint sweep found framework-shaped errors in new code (unbound methods, base-to-string, unsafe any, refs during render)
blockers.symptom: 41 ESLint errors across the new client/server/seed files, including `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method` for destructured `context.repository` in seeds, `no-base-to-string` for CSV/`String(...)` calls, `no-unsafe-*` from `Array.isArray` narrowing to `any[]`, and `react-hooks/refs` from writing a ref during render.
blockers.rootCause: Each is a strict-rule pattern the surrounding code must follow: `MigrationContext.repository` is a method signature (so destructuring detaches `this`); `Array.isArray` narrows to `any[]`; a ref may not be written during render.
blockers.resolution: Call `context.repository` off the context object, type `execute<T>()` for query rows, accept `string | number | null | undefined` in `csvEscape`, re-type the array after the `Array.isArray` guard, sync the ref in a `useEffect`, and move the form's pure helpers into `claim-form-model.ts` so the component file only exports components (Fast Refresh).

blockers.title: The shadcn-added client packages were moved in package.json but not in pnpm-lock.yaml, so frozen-lockfile verification failed
blockers.symptom: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` failed with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`: `@nocobase/i18n (lockfile: 1.0.0-beta.5, manifest: ^1.0.0-beta.5)`. After correcting that, it failed again because `@tanstack/react-table`, `date-fns` and `react-day-picker` sat in the lockfile importer`s `dependencies:` block while package.json declared them in `devDependencies:`.
blockers.rootCause: The shadcn CLI added the client packages to `dependencies` and pinned `@nocobase/i18n` to an exact range; the previous repair moved the three packages to `devDependencies` and restored the `^` in package.json, but never regenerated `pnpm-lock.yaml`, so its importer section still described the pre-move manifest.
blockers.resolution: Moved the three entries into the lockfile importer`s `devDependencies:` block in alphabetical position and restored `^1.0.0-beta.5` for `@nocobase/i18n`; confirmed with the exact verification command `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only --prefer-offline --ignore-scripts`.

improvements.title: Document that a seed must be load-safe: no relative .js import of another source file
improvements.detail: The seed loader rewrites only the entry file's relative import extension, and the in-process app-test path imports raw TypeScript with Node's type stripping. A seed that imports a sibling source module therefore loads via `tsx` but fails inside `createAppTest`, which is exactly where feature tests install seeds.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a short section to the application-development Skill's `references/migrations.md` (seeds): 'A seed is loaded as raw TypeScript; keep it self-contained. Do not import a sibling source module through a `.js` specifier — share nothing, or duplicate the small declaration.' Cross-link it from `references/testing.md`.

improvements.title: Document the CSRF trusted-origin requirement for cookie writes in tests
improvements.detail: An app test that writes through a session cookie fails with `INVALID_CSRF_ORIGIN` unless (a) the request carries a trusted `Origin` and (b) that origin is in `auth.trustedOrigins`. `TestSession.fetch` adds no `Origin`, so the two-part fix is not discoverable from the types.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add to the application-development Skill's `references/testing.md` (and the authentication plugin Skill) a tested snippet: `createAppTest({ config: { auth: { trustedOrigins: [TEST_ORIGIN] } } })` plus a `write()` helper that sets `origin` and `content-type`, and note that `createAppTest` also needs an explicit `auth.secret`.

improvements.title: createAppTest could provision a test auth secret and trusted origin by default
improvements.detail: Every authenticated feature test must rediscover that the app ships no default secret and that cookie writes need a trusted origin. The harness already provisions an isolated database and config; a default test secret and a trusted `TEST_ORIGIN` would remove a recurring, non-business obstacle.
improvements.suggestedChange: In `@nocobase/app-testing` `createTestAppConfig`, default `auth.secret` to a per-test random value and default `auth.trustedOrigins` to `[TEST_ORIGIN]` when unset, leaving both overridable through `config`.

improvements.title: Call out that the file plugin's content route is public and must be wrapped for private files
improvements.detail: `defineFileRepositoryApiRoutes` serves `${accessPath}/:file` without authentication: the UUID is the capability. An application storing private documents can, without noticing, expose them to anyone who learns or guesses the UUID.
improvements.suggestedChange: In the file plugin Skill's SKILL.md, add a prominent note: the generated content route is public; to protect it, scope an `auth.required()` middleware to your own `accessPath` prefix and record that byte-level per-record authorization is not provided by the plugin.

improvements.title: Document the public-base-path rule for hand-built request URLs in app tests
improvements.detail: Only `testApp.request()` adds `publicBasePath`; a root-level URL built by hand must include it or the standalone adapter answers 404. `publicBasePath` is also not a vitest fixture, so a bare reference is `undefined`.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add to `references/testing.md`: 'For a root-level path, build `` `http://localhost${testApp.publicBasePath}${path}` `` from the returned app; `publicBasePath` is not a fixture.'

improvements.title: The shadcn CLI puts client-only packages into dependencies
improvements.detail: Adding `@nocobase/data-table` and `@nocobase/date-picker` placed `@tanstack/react-table`, `date-fns`, `react-day-picker` and `cn` in `dependencies`, but by the template's deployment split all client imports belong in `devDependencies` (and `@nocobase/i18n` must stay a `^`-ranged dependency).
improvements.suggestedChange: Note in the application-development Skill's frontend `references/shadcn.md` that after every `shadcn add` the new client packages must be moved to `devDependencies` and `@nocobase/i18n`'s `^` range restored; consider a post-add check in the CLI.

improvements.title: ESLint strictness is only visible at the end of a feature
improvements.detail: The repository lints with `--max-warnings 0` and several type-aware rules (unbound-method, no-unsafe-*, no-base-to-string) fire on idiomatic framework calls. Running the lint sweep only after the feature is complete produced a 41-error backlog in one round.
improvements.suggestedChange: In the implement prompt, ask the agent to run `pnpm exec eslint` on each new file as it is written, or at least once before writing the tests, instead of only at the end.

improvements.title: Regenerate pnpm-lock.yaml after moving a package between dependency sections
improvements.detail: Editing package.json dependency sections without regenerating pnpm-lock.yaml leaves the lockfile importer mismatched. `--frozen-lockfile` is the first verification check, so it aborts the run and masks every later failure (format, lint, typecheck, test, build).
improvements.suggestedChange: After any `shadcn add`-driven package.json edit, run `pnpm install --lockfile-only` (or `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile`) so the lockfile importer records the correct section, then confirm with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts`.

- **`tags`**: the plugin name in PascalCase, such as `Hub`, `Users` or `AiEmployee`. The application's own routes tag the resource, such as `Orders`.
- **`summary`**: an English verb phrase, such as `Deploy an app`.
- **`operationId`**: the namespace, a verb and the resource in camelCase, unique across the application, such as `hubDeployApp`; the application's own routes have no namespace, `cancelOrder`.

- **Inputs**: `apiValidator()` for every path, query, header and JSON input, which documents the parameters and the body.
- **Responses**: `dataResponse(schema)` for `{ data }`, `listResponse(itemSchema, metaSchema?)` for `{ data, meta }`, `emptyResponse()` for a `204`, and the standard error body through `apiErrorResponse(status)` or `apiErrorResponse(409, 'When …')`. The rules are absolute, because these files are history that has already run on other machines:

- **Self-contained.** Spell out every table, field, index, constraint and metadata operation in the file. Never import a Collection definition, model, registry or shared constant that keeps evolving — that silently changes both the behavior and the checksum of something already applied.
- **Immutable once merged.** Check with `git log -- <file>` if unsure. Before the branch is merged you may correct the file in place; after it, every change is a new, later file. Never hard-code a previous checksum to make an edited migration look untouched. Correcting it in place changes nothing on its own — it is recorded as executed, so a plain apply skips it and the database keeps the schema the old file produced. `pnpm nocobase db redo` rolls the latest batch back and applies it again.
- **The file name body matches `name`**, and the name is unique across every source in the application.
- **Declare `irreversible: true`** when there is no real reverse operation, instead of writing a `down()` that quietly does nothing.
- **A seed is idempotent**, keyed on a stable business value backed by a unique constraint, so a repeated run is a no-op — `upsertOne` is the direct way to express that. A seed context has no `builder` at all, and a seed has no rollback or truncate behavior.

A backfill belongs in the migration that makes it necessary, using `query` from the same context — not in a seed.

Both run inside a transaction by default. `transaction: false` opts out, and a failure then leaves partial work behind with no history record, so take it only when the operation genuinely cannot run in one.

A task's `connection` is not the runtime connection either. It carries `dialect`, `capabilities` and `client()` — enough to branch on the database, and deliberately not a way back to the manager. Anything conditional on the dialect reads it from there.

`policy` is required and governs every action of the exposure, uploads included. It is a Repository Policy: `read`, `create`, `update` and `delete`, each `true`, `false`, or a rule node. A node that is `false` refuses that operation; a node with no `fields` accepts no caller-supplied field, which is what a metadata `createOne` needs before it will accept anything. Pass a function of the principal — `policy: (principal) => ({ ... })` — together with a `principal(context)` resolver to scope rows to the caller; without a principal the request is refused with 403.

An upload supplies no caller fields, so it binds a Policy derived from this one: the `create` scope and defaults are inherited and the field allowlist is replaced by the file columns. `create: false` therefore forbids uploading as well as creating metadata — decided, with the principal, before the body limit, the content type or the multipart body is read, so a refused upload answers `403 WRITE_FORBIDDEN` (domain `app`) and stores nothing — and a `create.defaults` of `{ ownerId }` is stamped onto uploaded rows — which is what keeps an uploaded file inside the same scope `findMany` reads. The content route under `accessPath` is the exception: it is public and this Policy does not reach it.

Content is GET `<accessPath>/<uuid>.<ext>` outside `/api`, omitting the dot when extensionless. Stream returns full bytes as an attachment; redirect returns a public storage URL or a five-minute signed URL. A disk without URL support requires stream mode; there is no automatic fallback.

These are public routes. For restricted files, register App-owned authentication and authorization on the paths each contribution owns before mounting it — `/<name>/<action>` per exposed API action, `<accessPath>/*` for content. Never `router.use('*', ...)` in a contribution router: contributions share the mounted router, so it also guards the SPA and every contribution mounted after yours. Check the operation and record/parent-record access; a login page, private disk, Client filter or Policy field allowlist is not authentication. Add scoped middleware and principal-based Policy to the generated routes first. If an existing contract needs an adapter, extend that module using the public Server manager and retain its authorization checks; missing built-in authentication alone is not a reason to replace the routes. Never trust browser-supplied ownership.
